title: ExecuteSQL reference without target
description: Error-prone rule — a table or field named in an ExecuteSQL statement that does not exist in the solution: the FROM/JOIN name matches no table occurrence of the file, a column matches no field of its table, or a formula reference inside the SQL points to a deleted field (<Field Missing>). FileMaker reports no error for this: ExecuteSQL simply returns ? and the calling logic works with an empty or wrong value.
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: Names inside the SQL text are invisible to FileMaker's own reference tracking. Renaming or deleting a table occurrence or field breaks the query silently — ExecuteSQL returns ?, and the error only surfaces as missing data at runtime.
rule.remediation: Restore or rename the table occurrence / field the query names, or build the names with GetFieldName / a name wrapper so that FileMaker tracks them.

meta.calibration: Built on CalculationSqlRefs (schema 1.42.0). System tables (FileMaker_Tables, FileMaker_Fields, FileMaker_BaseTables, FileMaker_BaseTableFields) are never findings. Names whose table cannot be determined (dynamic table name, ambiguous qualifier) are marked Low_Confidence and excluded — only references that are certainly broken are reported.
